html:
A historian and politician from Upper Volta, the first African to pass the French agregation in history (1956), and a founder of the writing of African history from African sources.

His History of Black Africa (1972) told the continent's past as more than a story of outsiders, and he edited the first volume of the UNESCO General History of Africa. He used oral tradition alongside written records, as did Cheikh Anta Diop. He was also an opposition leader at home, often in exile, and won the Right Livelihood Award in 1997. His motto was that one does not develop, one develops oneself. See also UNESCO.
